description: We are a team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, working on “Dancing with the SARs.” We aim to use satellite data and AI to detect changes on Earth. We welcome teammates with skills in AI/ML, Python, GIS, data analysis, and web development. Let's innovate and solve real-world problems together!
summary:
SAR-BRIDGE AI is an AI-powered environmental intelligence platform that transforms satellite radar observations into measurable, explainable, and actionable insights for water resource management.

Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Dancing with the SARs, our platform integrates NASA–ISRO NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar data, ESA Sentinel-2 imagery, and ERA5 environmental datasets to detect reservoir surface changes, investigate potential drivers, and support evidence-based decisions.

Our working prototype focuses on Azerbaijan's Mingachevir Reservoir, analyzing real NISAR observations from June and October 2026. Through interactive geospatial visualization, users can explore water gain and loss, measure affected areas, compare observations, and examine sector-level changes using an evidence-driven AI analysis engine.

What distinguishes SAR-BRIDGE AI is its human-centered, explainable approach. Rather than presenting AI-generated conclusions as facts, the system evaluates supporting and missing evidence, communicates uncertainty, and enables domain experts to validate findings before making decisions.

Designed for scalability, SAR-BRIDGE AI aims to expand into a broader environmental monitoring and decision-support platform for researchers, ecologists and water resource authorities worldwide.

Our mission: Beyond detecting change, we make satellite intelligence understandable, verifiable, and useful for human decisions.
details:
Overview

SAR-BRIDGE AI is an AI-powered environmental intelligence and decision-support platform designed to bridge the gap between satellite observations and practical water resource management.

Our platform transforms complex Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into measurable, explainable, and verifiable environmental insights, helping researchers, environmental scientists, and water resource authorities investigate reservoir changes.

How It Works

Our working prototype focuses on Azerbaijan's Mingachevir Reservoir, using real NASA–ISRO NISAR Level-2 GCOV observations from June and October 2026.

A Python-based geospatial processing pipeline analyzes HH and HV radar measurements, identifies water-to-land and land-to-water transitions, and calculates affected surface areas.

The results are presented through an interactive geospatial dashboard featuring before-and-after comparisons, water gain and loss visualization, and detailed analysis across ten monitoring sectors.

To strengthen scientific reliability, SAR-BRIDGE integrates ESA Sentinel-2 optical imagery for independent cross-sensor comparison and ERA5 environmental data for meteorological context.

AI and Innovation

What makes SAR-BRIDGE distinctive is its evidence-driven, explainable AI approach.

Rather than simply detecting changes or generating unsupported explanations, the system investigates possible environmental drivers, evaluates available supporting evidence, identifies missing information, and communicates uncertainty.

Our Human-in-the-Loop framework ensures that AI assists scientific investigation while domain experts retain responsibility for validating findings and making final decisions.

Technologies Used

The platform combines NASA Earthdata and Alaska Satellite Facility resources, NISAR SAR observations, Sentinel-2 imagery, ERA5/ERA5-Land reanalysis, Python-based geospatial processing, interactive web mapping, and AI-assisted evidence interpretation.

Impact and Future Development

SAR-BRIDGE aims to make Earth observation data more accessible and useful for environmental monitoring, scientific research, and water resource management.

Our current MVP demonstrates reservoir surface-change analysis at Mingachevir. Future development will focus on additional reservoirs, stronger ground-truth validation, automated data updates, and broader environmental monitoring capabilities.

Our vision is to transform satellite observations into transparent environmental intelligence that empowers human experts to make better-informed decisions.
